summary: The co-editing code at 2a5d2d8 (packages/collab with the page link and host relay; the fixes landed in 97d1fea) keeps every edit in the log exactly once, in one order, and loses none: all five frozen properties hold for 2 clients x 2 ops x 2 cuts (470,001 states), with late frames reaching the store (812,881 states), for 3 clients x 1 op x 2 cuts with liveness (1,161,825 states), and, safety and quiet-state P4, for 3 clients x 2 ops x 1 cut (90,240,507 states). The design as written still fails P4 in two ways (F1, F2); both are fixed in the code and pinned by scenarios. The drift step found no new violation.

modeled: Server (decide.ts, server.ts, store.ts at 2a5d2d8): compare-and-append with the (client, seq) duplicate check first; the attempt fence on resume hellos; welcome plus catch-up; superseding the client's other live sockets; ignoring closed sockets; ack to the sender, change to every other live socket

Engine (engine.ts): confirmed, one in-flight {seq, base, ops, doomed}, pending, nextSeq, the connection count sent as attempt; chunked submits (a prefix of pending); ack, change and stale rules with their protocol-error branches; reconnect, catch-up, resend or drop of the in-flight
Link (collab-link.ts, embed collab.ts): the connectId fence, so frames of a given-up socket never reach the engine

Environment: per-connection in-order channels; a cut at any moment loses undelivered frames toward the client; frames the client sent on a cut connection may reach the server later or never; concurrent submits
abstracted: Ops are opaque ids; integrate keeps ids and order (no rebasing semantics)
A change frame carries only its version; the client reads the immutable log[v]
Welcome plus the whole catch-up is one server step; decideSubmit plus store.append is one server step
Backoff is fairness, not time; only the current connection keeps a server-to-client queue
out_of_scope: Initial join (need_base, base, hello without resume), epoch reset and drop
save / saved / held changes, fingerprint, diverged, peers, canEdit = false, too_large, schema_mismatch
Single frames dropped or duplicated inside an open connection; frames of a closed socket reaching the engine
Two engines sharing a client id; page reloads; a non-atomic store; adapter transforms and exceptions
waitFor and held as variables (StaleAfterCatchUp shows waitFor never blocks; held needs save or a late attach)
store failures, the protocol-strike limit, a durable store
assumptions: A1: store.append is atomic per document and frames of a document are handled one at a time (memoryStore has no await in append; enqueue chains every frame); a durable store must keep this
A2: welcome and the whole catch-up go out before any live change on that socket (same chained task)
A3: frames of a closed link never reach the engine and vice versa: enforced by the connectId fence in collab-link.ts and embed collab.ts; another CollabLink must keep it
A4: a connection is in order and never drops or duplicates single frames without closing
A5: integrate keeps the op ids of local, in order
A6: one epoch, canEdit everywhere, no save, export or fingerprint, editor attached, store never fails; clients start welcomed at version 0
A7: one engine per client id
A8: MC_late (old sockets never closed, no fence) stands for a second server process sharing the store or a close the server has not noticed

findings.title: A late hello from a dead connection supersedes the live socket
findings.story: Design as written: client c2 drops (cut 1) and reconnects on connection 2 with hello {resume}. Connection 2 drops too before the server has read that hello (cut 2). c2 reconnects on connection 3. The server reads connection 3's hello first and welcomes it; then connection 2's hello arrives and, read as 'the second hello closes the older socket', supersedes the live connection 3. c2 fails with its edits unconfirmed (P4). The first code closed the socket accepted earlier, which behind a proxy that accepts connections out of order is the same bug. Fix in 97d1fea (unchanged at 2a5d2d8): hello.resume.attempt is the engine's connection count (engine.ts:286,295); decideHello answers superseded on that socket only when resume.attempt is below the highest attempt welcomed for the client (decide.ts:61-64), and welcome records the attempt (server.ts:403). The page link's connectId fence keeps that superseded away from the engine. The model now has exactly this rule (AttemptFence, welcomed); the as-written variant stays in the matrix and must fail. Reproduction: the scenario failing on the accept-order code is as reported by the implementer; this drift step ran the scenario only at HEAD, where it passes.

fix.summary: Fence resume hellos by a per-client connection attempt number (hello.resume.attempt) instead of accept order.

findings.title: A doomed in-flight left over a reconnect blocks every later submit
findings.story: Design as written: c1 submits {seq 1, base 0} and its link drops before any answer. c1 reconnects and is welcomed at head 0. c2's submit becomes version 1 and reaches c1 during catch-up as a foreign change, which dooms c1's in-flight. Section 5 says only what happens to an in-flight that is not doomed; the stale that would clear the doomed one went to the dead connection. With an in-flight present nothing is sent again, and c1's edit stays in pending (P4). The engine was written with the fix: caughtUp drops a doomed in-flight and the next submit reuses its seq (engine.ts:475). The design-as-written variant (DoomedOnReconnect = "keep") stays in the matrix and must fail. Reproduction: no engine without the fix ever existed, so there is no failing run; the scenario drives the F2 schedule and passes at HEAD.

reproduction.test: packages/collab/tests/scenarios.test.ts::schedules found by the protocol model (formal/collab-protocol) F2: a submit cut off with its connection and doomed during catch-up goes out again with its seq

fix.summary: After catch-up a doomed in-flight is dropped (its ops are already in pending) and the next submit reuses its seq. The engine had this from its first version; the scenario pins it.
fix.diff:
engine.ts:474-475
   const inflight = s.inflight
   if (inflight?.doomed) s.inflight = null

doomed; no stale will ever come

simplifications.change: The (client, seq) duplicate check in store.append
simplifications.justification: With engines that follow section 5 it never decides anything: every copy of a seq still on the wire has the same base, and a copy with another base is sent only after invariant 5 proved the old one dead, so base === head already rejects the second copy (EQUIVALENT mutant under MC_late.cfg). Against an engine that replays an appended seq with the current head as base, it is the only thing that keeps invariant 2 and P1 (DETECTED under MC_rogue.cfg).

simplifications.change: The seq comparison in the lost-ack rule ("change mine with seq === inflight.seq")
simplifications.justification: An own change at confirmed + 1 always carries the in-flight seq (FramesCovered holds everywhere; EQUIVALENT mutant under MC.cfg and MC_late.cfg). Keep it: it costs nothing and turns a server bug into a protocol error instead of a wrong confirmation.

simplifications.change: The "if not doomed" branch of the stale rule and the wait "until confirmed >= stale.head"
simplifications.justification: NoStaleForLiveInflight and StaleAfterCatchUp hold in every passing config: a stale always finds its in-flight doomed and the client already at stale.head, because the server sends every change up to stale.head before the stale on that socket. Implementers may write the branch as an assertion or a logged protocol error rather than as a resend path.
